fixture: fixtures/ — Widgets feature PR (mini-repo mirroring server/src/)
prompt: Review this PR for Onion architecture / ring-boundary violations. The changed files are in evals/fixtures/: contracts/widgets.ts, adapters/llm/openai-tagger.ts, platform/container.ts (excerpt), platform/errors.ts (context only), and the feature module widgets/ (routes.ts, service.ts, repository.ts). For each problem: name the exact ring rule it breaks and say which file the fix goes in. Do not pad the list with speculative issues; if a file is fine, leave it alone.

findings.location: constructor(private readonly container: Container) + platform/container.ts `new WidgetsService(this)`
must_name: service takes the Container instead of the ports it uses (and reaches for `this.container.widgetTagger()` at call time — a service-locator lookup instead of an injected port)
the container also constructs it, so this is a real no-circular / dependency cycle (arch:check will fail), not just a testability smell
fix: a WidgetsDeps-style object of the specific ports (repo + WidgetTagger), assembled by the container — the repo-intel / blast / brief pattern

findings.location: imports db/client + db/schema/widgets; db.insert(...).returning() in create(), db.select()...offset() in list()
findings.rule: SKILL rule 1 (direction) / stack-rules 'Drizzle stops at repository.ts' / service-not-in-db
must_name: the application ring runs Drizzle queries directly
the injected repository is bypassed for create/list (only get() uses it) — two data-access paths
fix: move the insert and the list query into WidgetsRepository methods; the service keeps only the decisions

findings.location: imports WidgetsRepository; `new WidgetsRepository(container.db())`; `repo.countAll()` in the GET handler
findings.rule: SKILL rule 1 (direction) — 'routes.ts may not import repository.ts'
must_name: the entry ring talks to the repository directly, bypassing the service
fix: the service returns the list data (count included); routes never import or construct the repository

findings.location: `body: z.unknown()` schema + `const body = CreateWidget.parse(req.body)` in the POST handler
findings.rule: stack-rules (Fastify) / anti-pattern 6 — validate with the route schema, not .parse() in the handler
must_name: validation is done in the handler with .parse() instead of `schema.body`
fix: `schema: { body: CreateWidget }`; the handler receives an already-valid DTO

findings.location: findById(): Promise<WidgetRow | undefined> and listStaleUntagged(): Promise<WidgetRow[]>; service.get() returns the row as Widget
findings.rule: stack-rules (Drizzle) / anti-pattern 3 — repository returns a domain type; row types stay in infrastructure
must_name: the Drizzle row type (WidgetRow from db/rows.ts) escapes the repository and reaches the application ring
fix: map to the domain Widget inside the repository (move toWidget there)

findings.location: listStaleUntagged() encodes the 'stale' rule (STALE_AFTER_DAYS cutoff + untagged) in the SQL where-clause
findings.rule: stack-rules (Drizzle) 'no business logic in a repository' / anti-pattern 4 / decision-tree 'business logic that needs the DB'
must_name: 'what counts as stale' is a business policy sitting in the persistence ring
fix: the decision lives in the service; the repository takes the cutoff as a parameter / runs the query it is told to
the port imports an `openai` SDK type into the innermost ring and speaks the vendor's vocabulary — a wrapper, not a port
fix: a domain-named port (e.g. `suggest(name: string): Promise<string[]>` or a small domain input); the OpenAI types stay inside the adapter

findings.rule: SKILL rule 2 — a port the client has no use for goes in server/src/ports/
must_name: widget tagging is server-only; the browser bundle never tags a widget, so the port must not land in the vendored `vendor/shared` type surface
fix: put the port in server/src/ports/ (same innermost ring, not vendored) — the Widget / CreateWidget contracts legitimately stay in vendor/shared

findings.location: WidgetsPage = { items, page, pageSize, total, nextCursor }
findings.rule: stack-rules (Zod) — a contract schema describes the domain shape, not a transport envelope; pagination/HTTP framing stays in routes.ts
must_name: the pagination envelope (page/pageSize/total/nextCursor) is baked into a domain contract
fix: the contract is the domain list; routes.ts wraps the transport envelope (assembling it in the handler is fine)

findings.rule: stack-rules (DI container) / repo secrets convention — adapters are constructed lazily and resolved through SecretsProvider; secrets never read from env/AppConfig/DB in adapter code
must_name: the adapter reaches into process.env for its key instead of receiving it
fix: take the key (or a configured client) as a constructor argument; platform/container.ts resolves it via SecretsProvider when it lazily builds the adapter

minor_notes_ok: platform/container.ts reads this.overrides.widgets but ContainerOverrides only declares widgetTagger? — the `widgets?` field is missing (untestable by substitution).
widgetsRoutes constructs `new WidgetsService(container)` in the route file rather than the container (same debt as the repo's own repos/agents/reviews modules).
